title: Configure and verify NTP operating in client and server mode

questions.question: Which command allow your router to synchronize with a time source of 129.6.15.28?

correct.explanation: NTP server is configured in global config mode: ntp server 129.6.15.28 — synchronizes router clock to the stratum source.

incorrect.explanation: NTP server is not an exec-mode command — configuration belongs under configure terminal.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: NTP server in privileged exec instead of config mode
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#ntp server 129.6.15.28 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for synchronize.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "synchronize", Router(config)#ntp server 129.6.15.28 satisfies what this question tests — Router#ntp server 129.6.15.28 does not.

incorrect.explanation: ntp client is not the IOS command to point at an NTP server — use ntp server <ip>.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#ntp client 129.6.15.28 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for synchronize.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "synchronize", Router(config)#ntp server 129.6.15.28 satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#ntp client 129.6.15.28 does not.

incorrect.explanation: Exec-mode ntp client is invalid — NTP peers/servers are defined in configuration mode.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#ntp client 129.6.15.28 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for synchronize.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "synchronize", Router(config)#ntp server 129.6.15.28 satisfies what this question tests — Router#ntp client 129.6.15.28 does not.

answerReview.examTip: NTP: ntp server <ip> in global config. Verify with show ntp associations.

questions.question: Which command configures the router or switch to trust its internal time clock?

correct.explanation: ntp master configures the device to act as an authoritative NTP time source using its system clock.

incorrect.explanation: ntp server points to an upstream NTP peer — it does not declare this device as the master clock.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Using ntp server to become time master
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#ntp server points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for configures.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "configures", Router(config)#ntp master satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#ntp server does not.

incorrect.explanation: ntp clock source is not standard syntax for designating the local device as master.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#ntp clock source points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for configures.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "configures", Router(config)#ntp master satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#ntp clock source does not.

incorrect.explanation: ntp trusted marks peers as trusted for ACL purposes — it does not make the router the master clock.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Confusing ntp trusted with ntp master
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#ntp trusted points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for configures.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "configures", Router(config)#ntp master satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#ntp trusted does not.

answerReview.examTip: Device is the time authority → ntp master (after setting clock or syncing once).

questions.question: Which command can see if the router or switch is using NTP?

correct.explanation: show clock detail reveals whether time is NTP-synchronized or manually set — shows source and stratum.

incorrect.explanation: show ntp alone is incomplete — show clock detail confirms NTP sync status.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#show ntp points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for the router or switch is using NTP.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "the router or switch is using NTP", Router#show clock detail satisfies what this question tests — Router#show ntp does not.

incorrect.explanation: show time is not a valid Cisco IOS command.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#show time points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for the router or switch is using NTP.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "the router or switch is using NTP", Router#show clock detail satisfies what this question tests — Router#show time does not.

incorrect.explanation: show time source does not exist — use show clock detail.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#show time source points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for the router or switch is using NTP.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "the router or switch is using NTP", Router#show clock detail satisfies what this question tests — Router#show time source does not.

answerReview.examTip: NTP sync check: show clock detail (synced vs unsynced) | show ntp status for stratum.

questions.question: Which command can view the time details from a configured server?

correct.explanation: show ntp associations detail shows configured NTP servers, reachability, stratum, and offset per peer.

incorrect.explanation: show clock detail shows local clock sync status — not per-server association details.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: show clock detail for server associations
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#show clock detail points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for configured.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "configured", Router#show ntp associations detail satisfies what this question tests — Router#show clock detail does not.

incorrect.explanation: show ntp detail is not the standard command — use show ntp associations detail.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#show ntp detail points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for configured.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "configured", Router#show ntp associations detail satisfies what this question tests — Router#show ntp detail does not.

incorrect.explanation: show ntp skew is not valid IOS — server details are in show ntp associations detail.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#show ntp skew points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for configured.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "configured", Router#show ntp associations detail satisfies what this question tests — Router#show ntp skew does not.

answerReview.examTip: NTP verify: show ntp associations (summary) | detail for per-server stratum/offset/reach.

questions.question: Which protocol and port does NTP use for time synchronization by default?

correct.explanation: NTP uses UDP port 123 for time synchronization — not TCP and not SNMP (161) or TFTP (69).

incorrect.explanation: UDP/161 is SNMP — NTP is UDP/123.
incorrect.whatItDoes: TCP/161 states an IPv6 address, prefix length, or assignment method that may not follow shortening rules.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Transport protocol (protocol): UDP/123 matches reliability, ports, or connection behavior — TCP/161 picks the wrong L4 protocol or port role.

incorrect.explanation: NTP is UDP-based, not TCP — and port 123, not 161.
incorrect.whatItDoes: TCP/123 states an IPv6 address, prefix length, or assignment method that may not follow shortening rules.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Transport protocol (protocol): UDP/123 matches reliability, ports, or connection behavior — TCP/123 picks the wrong L4 protocol or port role.

incorrect.explanation: UDP/69 is TFTP — NTP uses UDP/123.
incorrect.whatItDoes: UDP/69 states an IPv6 address, prefix length, or assignment method that may not follow shortening rules.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Transport protocol (protocol): UDP/123 matches reliability, ports, or connection behavior — UDP/69 picks the wrong L4 protocol or port role.

answerReview.examTip: NTP = UDP/123 | SNMP = UDP/161 (agent) / UDP/162 (traps) | memorize the UDP service ports.

questions.question: Which command help you diagnose if the router or switch is getting an answer back from an NTP server?

correct.explanation: debug ntp packets shows NTP packet exchange — confirms whether the device receives replies from the server.

incorrect.explanation: show ntp alone is incomplete — use show ntp status or debug ntp packets for reachability.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Truncated show ntp for server response
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#show ntp points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for the router or switch is getting an answer back from an NTP server.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "the router or switch is getting an answer back from an NTP server", Router#debug ntp packets satisfies what this question tests — Router#show ntp does not.

incorrect.explanation: show ip ntp is not valid IOS — use show ntp status or debug ntp packets.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#show ip ntp is a verification command that inspects a different table or feature than the stem asks about.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "the router or switch is getting an answer back from an NTP server", Router#debug ntp packets satisfies what this question tests — Router#show ip ntp does not.

incorrect.explanation: debug ntp messages logs event messages — debug ntp packets inspects actual NTP request/reply traffic.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: NTP messages debug for packet exchange
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#debug ntp messages points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for the router or switch is getting an answer back from an NTP server.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "the router or switch is getting an answer back from an NTP server", Router#debug ntp packets satisfies what this question tests — Router#debug ntp messages does not.

answerReview.examTip: NTP troubleshoot: show ntp associations → show ntp status → debug ntp packets (disable debug when done).

questions.question: Which is a best practice for setting up NTP?
choices: Always configure the time source to a DNS address.
Configure all devices to a public NTP server.
Configure all devices to different NTP servers for redundancy.
Configure all devices as master servers.

correct.explanation: Use a DNS hostname for the NTP server — if the server's IP changes, devices follow the name without reconfiguration.

incorrect.explanation: Pointing every device at one public server is fragile — use internal stratum sources or enterprise NTP hierarchy.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: All devices to one public NTP server
incorrect.whatItDoes: Configure all devices to a public NTP server. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for practice.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "practice", Always configure the time source to a DNS address. satisfies what this question tests — Configure all devices to a public NTP server. does not.

incorrect.explanation: Different NTP servers per device causes clock drift inconsistency — synchronize to a common stratum source.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Per-device different NTP servers for redundancy
incorrect.whatItDoes: Configure all devices to different NTP servers for redundancy. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for practice.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "practice", Always configure the time source to a DNS address. satisfies what this question tests — Configure all devices to different NTP servers for redundancy. does not.

incorrect.explanation: Only one authoritative source should be master — end devices should be NTP clients, not masters.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Configure all devices as master servers. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for practice.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "practice", Always configure the time source to a DNS address. satisfies what this question tests — Configure all devices as master servers. does not.

answerReview.examTip: NTP best practice: DNS name for the server + hierarchical stratum (client → internal server → public stratum-1).

correct.explanation: show ntp status displays clock offset, stratum, and time drift relative to the reference.

incorrect.explanation: show ntp is incomplete — drift/offset details are in show ntp status.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#show ntp points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for observed.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "observed", Router#show ntp status satisfies what this question tests — Router#show ntp does not.

incorrect.explanation: show ip ntp status is not valid IOS — use show ntp status.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Invented show ip ntp status command
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#show ip ntp status is a verification command that inspects a different table or feature than the stem asks about.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Verification command (observed): Router#show ntp status inspects the right table or state — Router#show ip ntp status shows unrelated information.

incorrect.explanation: debug ntp drift does not exist — use show ntp status for offset/drift.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#debug ntp drift points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for observed.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "observed", Router#show ntp status satisfies what this question tests — Router#debug ntp drift does not.

answerReview.examTip: NTP drift/offset: show ntp status | Per-peer detail: show ntp associations detail.

questions.question: Which command sets the time zone of a router for Pacific Standard Time?

correct.explanation: clock timezone pst -8 0 sets Pacific Standard Time — offset -8 hours, no DST offset (second value 0).

incorrect.explanation: Timezone requires numeric offset — clock timezone pst -8 0, not a name alone.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#clock timezone pacific points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for standard.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "standard", Router(config)#clock timezone pst -8 0 satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#clock timezone pacific does not.

incorrect.explanation: timezone is not a valid global config command — use clock timezone.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#timezone pacific points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for standard.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "standard", Router(config)#clock timezone pst -8 0 satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#timezone pacific does not.

incorrect.explanation: timezone pst -8 is wrong syntax — IOS uses clock timezone <name> <offset-hours> <offset-minutes>.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#timezone pst -8 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for standard.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "standard", Router(config)#clock timezone pst -8 0 satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#timezone pst -8 does not.

answerReview.examTip: Timezone: clock timezone EST -5 0 | PST = -8 0 | PDT adds DST offset in second field.

questions.question: You are configuring NTP on your switch. You want to configure the switch so if any interface fails, NTP will still be available. Which type of interface should you use? Choose the best answer.

correct.explanation: A loopback interface stays up even if physical interfaces fail — NTP source binding remains reachable.

incorrect.explanation: Tunnel interfaces depend on underlying transport — not the stable NTP source choice.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Tunnel interface points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for any interface fails, NTP will still be available.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "any interface fails, NTP will still be available", Loopback interface satisfies what this question tests — Tunnel interface does not.

incorrect.explanation: NTP interface is not a Cisco interface type — use loopback.
incorrect.whatItDoes: NTP interface points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for any interface fails, NTP will still be available.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "any interface fails, NTP will still be available", Loopback interface satisfies what this question tests — NTP interface does not.

incorrect.explanation: SVI ties NTP to a VLAN — if that VLAN's L3 path fails, NTP source may drop.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: SVI over loopback for NTP resilience
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switched Virtual Interface (SVI) describes an inter-VLAN routing approach (SVI or router-on-a-stick) that may not fit this topology.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Inter-VLAN routing (any interface fails, NTP will still be available): Loopback interface provides L3 between VLANs — Switched Virtual Interface (SVI) leaves traffic unrouted or uses the wrong L3 interface.

answerReview.examTip: Stable NTP source: ntp source loopback0 — loopback is always up if the router is reachable.

questions.question: Which command configure NTP to use the internal loopback interface?

correct.explanation: ntp source loopback 0 binds outbound NTP packets to Loopback0 — survives physical interface failures.

incorrect.explanation: ntp loopback 0 is not valid syntax — use ntp source loopback 0.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#ntp loopback 0 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for configure.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "configure", Switch(config)#ntp source loopback 0 satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config)#ntp loopback 0 does not.

incorrect.explanation: ntp master makes this device a time server — ntp source only sets the source interface.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#ntp master loopback 0 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for configure.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "configure", Switch(config)#ntp source loopback 0 satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config)#ntp master loopback 0 does not.

incorrect.explanation: ntp clock is not a valid command — source interface uses ntp source.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#ntp clock loopback 0 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for configure.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "configure", Switch(config)#ntp source loopback 0 satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config)#ntp clock loopback 0 does not.

answerReview.examTip: NTP source: ntp source Loopback0 in global config — pairs with a configured loopback IP.

questions.question: Which command set the router’s internal clock to 2:24 August 1, 2019?

correct.explanation: clock set runs in privileged EXEC (Router#) — format: hours:minutes:seconds day month year.

incorrect.explanation: clock set is not a config-mode command — execute it from privileged EXEC (#).
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#clock set 2:24:00 1 august 2019 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for internal.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "internal", Router#clock set 2:24:00 1 august 2019 satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#clock set 2:24:00 1 august 2019 does not.

incorrect.explanation: Month/day order is day month — 1 august 2019, not august 1 2019.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Wrong clock set date field order
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#clock set 2:24:00 august 1 2019 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for internal.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "internal", Router#clock set 2:24:00 1 august 2019 satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#clock set 2:24:00 august 1 2019 does not.

incorrect.explanation: Missing set keyword — correct syntax is clock set <time> <day> <month> <year>.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#clock 2:24:00 1 august 2019 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for internal.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "internal", Router#clock set 2:24:00 1 august 2019 satisfies what this question tests — Router#clock 2:24:00 1 august 2019 does not.

answerReview.examTip: Manual time: Router# clock set HH:MM:SS DD MONTH YYYY — required before SSH key generation if NTP is down.
